quote: I arrived with my pockets full of nothing and the honest calculation that followed.
I walked out with a small packet in my palm and a larger accounting on my shoulders.
I folded the Contract into my pocket the way you fold a receipt for a transaction that you do not plan to return.
The bargain I had made was practical and unsentimental: room, work, a roof, and ten years of measured claims.
My humor about it was small and private. I told myself the trade was sensible.

value: has been provided shelter at the Mercy Academy (first night in clean bed)
quote: That night, when I lay in my clean bed for the first time in months, I thought of the Folio's blank lines and the Headmistress's closing line, and I felt the arithmetic of my choice settle down into the room: a tidy sum, a term, and a witness.
I slept that night with the plank floor under me and three new people breathing close.
I kept my contract in the inside pocket of my shirt and my humor small.
Rue stood at the end of one bench, the packet of papers heavy in her hands, the Contract itself wrapped in waxed cloth.

When the clerk folded the Contract away, tucking it in the same waxed cloth, Rue did not know whether she had chosen mercy or ledger. She only knew what she had traded: a name, a year, the small liberties of an unrecorded life. Her heel scraped the floor as she left the bench; the Hall kept going, businesslike and slow, the Folio closed like a chest.
She did not write her age. She hesitated, feeling the shape of her life as if it were a ledger to be balanced: a small credit here, a small debt there.

value: to bind herself under the Academy's terms (accept the Contract)
quote: She had practiced the weight of the decision in the hours when the city around the island was nothing but a smear of smoke and doorframes: how it felt to fold a life into a ledger, to press one's name so it would not lift again.
Rue had a place that night between two trunks and a girl who kept folding the corner of her sleeve until it was nervous and neat.
Rue fell asleep with Aya's hand warm by her elbow and the Bell's clear note sitting under all that closeness like a seal.

value: to understand and adapt to the House's systems
quote: In the dark she thought of how the house counted things: work, witness, record.
In the afternoons, Rue practiced stitches until her hands were small machines.

value: tools and smells of trade (needle, thread; hands smelling of sap and stitch)
quote: Walking back through the courtyard with her palms smelling faintly of sap and stitch, Rue thought of the seal behind glass and of the Three's stories braided into the beds.
In the afternoons, Rue practiced stitches until her hands were small machines.
She kept her hands busy and, as always, the ledger watched.

Rue kept the family ledger folded beneath the mattress of the ferry bed for a week after she left. At night she would open it by lamplight and trace the cramped lines, the pencilled sums and the pencilled coughs.
She had traded the small freedoms of being uncounted for a place that would teach her how to count and how to be counted.
Rue listened the way she had learned to listen in the classrooms—quiet, counting the gaps between the sentences.

value: to discover how promises and margins are enforced/what costs entail
quote: She left with more questions than she had when she entered.
